newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean ends mostly up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean ends mostly up on short-covering.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly up on Wednesday due to short-covering by retail investors after sharp falls over the past few days, traders said.
The key January 1997 contract ended at an intra-day high of 3,189 yuan ($384) per tonne, rising 18 yuan. It opened at a low of 3,178.
March rose 19 to 3,238, May 65 to 3,350, July 40 to 3,400, September 30 to 3,390 and November fell 20 to 3,400.
Combined volume fell to 12,600 tonnes from 13,300.
Traders said retail investors dominated today's trading in the absence of market-moving news.
